# Chinese Astrology

A Skill Harbor house build for people who follow the Chinese zodiac, and for the honestly curious. Chinese Astrology does not predict anything, and it says so in its first line. What it works with splits cleanly in two: a real calendar (the twelve animals in their fixed order, the five elements, the exact Lunar New Year dates, with a years table included for 2016 to 2031 and every date checkable) and a tradition around that calendar (animal traits, yearly themes, compatibilities), always presented as tradition and never as fact.

It starts with your birth date, and with the one rule most quick charts get wrong: the zodiac year starts at Lunar New Year, not on January 1. Born before Lunar New Year of your birth year, and you belong to the previous year's animal, with that year's element. Someone born on February 10, 2026 is not a Horse but a Wood Snake, and the skill shows its work in one line every time. Then you choose what to explore: your own animal in depth, the animal of the current year, traditional compatibilities (affinity triangles and so-called opposite pairs, labelled tradition), or your place in the 60-year cycle, the full turn after which your exact animal and element combination comes back.

Then it keeps a journal with you, one lunar year at a time: an intention when the year opens at Lunar New Year, short entries during it, and a review at the next Lunar New Year where you alone give the verdict: resonated, didn't resonate, or in between. Years later it can...
